Notre-Dame (Our Lady) of Paris is a magnificent cathedral.
fr_notre_dame_noun.why: U1 follow-up: Notre-Dame = the framed cathedral picture; example glossed.

fr_devotion_noun.why: U1 hook_lint: example carries the gloss.

fr_rosaire_noun.why: U1 follow-up: rosaire = the family of three in the pew.

fr_messe_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in eglise/sanctuaire (Nov 1 2026 EGLISE1 build): a small boy altar server in a white robe on his knees amid a big mess of about ten spilled blue hymnbooks scattered across the stone step, one hand on his forehead, gathering them up.
fr_messe_noun.note: La messe is the Catholic Mass (aller à la messe). Une messe can also be a musical Mass (la Messe en si de Bach).

fr_communion_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in eglise/sanctuaire (Nov 1 2026 EGLISE1 build): girl twirling in a white First Communion dress and veil.
fr_communion_noun.note: This is a cognate: it looks and sounds close to the English word, so the picture simply shows it. La communion is Holy Communion; la première communion is First Communion. It also means communion in general (en communion avec la nature).

fr_hostie_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in eglise/sanctuaire (Nov 1 2026 EGLISE1 build): gray-haired sacristan holding up one round white wafer, a gold plate of wafers and a gold tin on her side table.
fr_hostie_noun.note: This is a cognate: it looks and sounds close to the English word, so the picture simply shows it. L'hostie is the Host, the round wafer of the Eucharist. In Quebec French 'hostie' is also used as a swear word; in France it only means the Host.

fr_homelie_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in eglise/sanctuaire (Nov 1 2026 EGLISE1 build): a kind gray-haired priest in a black cassock with a white collar, walking slowly while reading aloud from two handwritten sheets of paper, one finger raised as he practices. Moved from the planned room R_ch_altar_02_z2 (not yet built) into this room.
fr_homelie_noun.note: This is a cognate: it looks and sounds close to the English word, so the picture simply shows it. L'homélie is the homily, the priest's short sermon after the readings. Figuratively, a long boring lecture (une homélie sur la politesse).

fr_autel_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in eglise/sanctuaire (Nov 1 2026 EGLISE1 build): a young hotel bellhop in a bright red uniform with gold buttons and a little red pillbox cap pushing a shiny brass hotel luggage cart loaded with pots of white lilies up to the plain stone altar with its white linen cloth.
fr_autel_noun.note: L'autel is the altar. Same sound as l'hôtel (hotel): only the spelling differs.

fr_tabernacle_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in eglise/sanctuaire (Nov 1 2026 EGLISE1 build): a small gilded box-shaped tabernacle with a little arched gold door, standing on a carved stone pillar behind the altar, a woman in a green cardigan dusting it with a feather duster. Moved from the planned room R_ch_altar_02_z1 (not yet built) into this room.
fr_tabernacle_noun.note: This is a cognate: it looks and sounds close to the English word, so the picture simply shows it. Le tabernacle is the small locked cupboard that keeps the Host. In Quebec French 'tabarnak' is a swear word; in France it only means the tabernacle.

fr_crucifix_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in eglise/sanctuaire (Nov 1 2026 EGLISE1 build): a teenage altar server in a white robe setting a tall plain wooden processional cross on a pole into a wooden floor stand; the cross carries a very small, simple, serene carved figure, no blood or wounds.
fr_crucifix_noun.note: This is a cognate: it looks and sounds close to the English word, so the picture simply shows it. Un crucifix is a cross with the figure of Christ; a plain cross is une croix.

fr_lectionnaire_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in eglise/sanctuaire (Nov 1 2026 EGLISE1 build): a young woman with a dark ponytail in a plain blue dress standing at a carved wooden lectern, reading aloud from a very large book with a gold cover and red ribbon markers. Moved from the planned room R_ch_altar_02_z1 (not yet built) into this room.
fr_lectionnaire_noun.note: This is a cognate: it looks and sounds close to the English word, so the picture simply shows it. Le lectionnaire is the book of Bible readings for each Mass.

fr_calice_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in eglise/sanctuaire (Nov 1 2026 EGLISE1 build): a teenage girl altar server in a white robe in the foreground polishing a shining gold chalice cup with a white cloth, sitting on a low wooden stool. Moved from the planned room R_ch_altar_02_z1 (not yet built) into this room.
fr_calice_noun.note: This is a cognate: it looks and sounds close to the English word, so the picture simply shows it. Le calice is the chalice, the cup used at Mass; in botany, the calyx of a flower. Boire le calice jusqu'à la lie: to drink the bitter cup to the dregs (to suffer to the end).

fr_crypte_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in eglise/crypte (Nov 1 2026 EGLISE1 build): small boy in a yellow sweater at the foot of the crypt steps, looking around.
fr_crypte_noun.note: La crypte is the crypt, the vaulted room under a church.

fr_relique_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in eglise/crypte (Nov 1 2026 EGLISE1 build): a woman tour guide in a green jacket pointing with an open hand at an old worn wooden walking staff standing in a lit arched wall niche.
fr_relique_noun.note: This is a cognate: it looks and sounds close to the English word, so the picture simply shows it. Une relique is a relic of a saint; also any treasured old keepsake (une relique de famille).

fr_sainte_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in eglise/crypte (Nov 1 2026 EGLISE1 build): a faded old wall fresco on the vault of a gentle woman saint in a long blue robe with a simple gold halo holding a small white lamb, a girl in a red coat gazing up at it.
fr_sainte_noun.note: This is a cognate: it looks and sounds close to the English word, so the picture simply shows it. Une sainte is a female saint; un saint, a male saint. As an adjective: la Sainte Vierge, la semaine sainte (Holy Week).

fr_benediction_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in eglise/crypte (Nov 1 2026 EGLISE1 build): a kind gray-haired priest in a black cassock raising his right hand in blessing over an elderly couple who bow their heads, smiling.
fr_benediction_noun.note: La bénédiction is a blessing (also figuratively: cette pluie est une bénédiction, this rain is a blessing). Close to English 'benediction'.

fr_eternel_adj.why: English sound-alike painted in eglise/crypte (Nov 1 2026 EGLISE1 build): a small red glass oil lamp hanging on a long brass chain from the vault, its little flame burning.
fr_eternel_adj.note: This is a cognate: it looks and sounds close to the English word, so the picture simply shows it. Éternel means eternal, everlasting; in everyday speech also 'endless' or 'perpetual' (ses éternelles excuses, his endless excuses).

fr_prier_verb.why: English sound-alike painted in eglise/crypte (Nov 1 2026 EGLISE1 build): Monsieur Verbe, a cheerful slim mime with white face paint, a black-and-white horizontally striped shirt, black suspenders, black trousers, white gloves and a red beret, little motion lines around his hands, kneeling quietly on the stone floor with his white-gloved hands folded and his eyes closed, praying peacefully. Moved from the planned room ST_faith_seg001 (not yet built) into this room.
fr_prier_verb.note: Prier means to pray (prier pour quelqu'un), and also to ask, to beg politely: je vous en prie (please, you're welcome), prier quelqu'un de partir (to ask someone to leave).

fr_honorer_verb.why: English sound-alike painted in eglise/crypte (Nov 1 2026 EGLISE1 build): Monsieur Verbe, a cheerful slim mime with white face paint, a black-and-white horizontally striped shirt, black suspenders, black trousers, white gloves and a red beret, little motion lines around his hands, bowing deeply and laying a bouquet of white flowers before the gilded reliquary. Moved from the planned room ST_emotion_seg013 (not yet built) into this room.
fr_honorer_verb.note: This is a cognate: it looks and sounds close to the English word, so the picture simply shows it. Honorer: to honor (honorer un saint, honorer sa parole, to keep one's word); also to pay a bill or a check (honorer une facture).

fr_reliquaire_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in eglise/crypte (Nov 1 2026 EGLISE1 build): a small gilded reliquary shaped like a tiny house with a pointed roof and little round crystal windows, standing on a small stone altar with two candles.
fr_reliquaire_noun.note: This is a cognate: it looks and sounds close to the English word, so the picture simply shows it. Un reliquaire is the decorated box that holds a relic.

fr_martyr_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in eglise/crypte (Nov 1 2026 EGLISE1 build): a carved stone relief on a thick round pillar showing a young saint in a long robe holding a palm branch, a calm peaceful smile, simple halo, two visitors admiring it.
fr_martyr_noun.note: This is a cognate: it looks and sounds close to the English word, so the picture simply shows it. Un martyr (une martyre) is a martyr; a palm branch is the martyr's sign in art. Also figuratively: jouer les martyrs, to play the martyr.

fr_pitie_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in eglise/confessionnal (Nov 1 2026 EGLISE1 build): a kind old lady in a brown coat crouching to wrap a small shivering wet gray kitten in her red wool scarf, a sad tender look on her face.
fr_pitie_noun.note: La pitié is pity. Avoir pitié de quelqu'un: to take pity on someone. Careful: faire pitié can be negative, 'to be pitiful' (c'est à faire pitié, it's pathetic). Sans pitié: merciless.

fr_confession_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in eglise/confessionnal (Nov 1 2026 EGLISE1 build): a little girl with brown chocolate smudged on her chin and fingers, looking down sheepishly while telling her grandmother something, the grandmother on a bench raising her eyebrows with a half smile.
fr_confession_noun.note: This is a cognate: it looks and sounds close to the English word, so the picture simply shows it. Une confession is a confession, both the sacrament and any admission (la confession d'un secret). Also a religious denomination (de confession catholique).

fr_reconciliation_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in eglise/confessionnal (Nov 1 2026 EGLISE1 build): two little brothers about six and eight hugging each other warmly, one with a slightly ruffled collar, a smiling woman teacher with glasses standing behind them.
fr_reconciliation_noun.note: This is a cognate: it looks and sounds close to the English word, so the picture simply shows it. La réconciliation is making up after a quarrel; in church, the sacrament of reconciliation is confession.

fr_contrition_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in eglise/confessionnal (Nov 1 2026 EGLISE1 build): a boy about nine hanging his head, truly sorry, holding out the broken pieces of a small terracotta flowerpot with a red geranium in both hands.
fr_contrition_noun.note: This is a cognate: it looks and sounds close to the English word, so the picture simply shows it. La contrition is deep sorrow for having done wrong (close to English contrite).

fr_pardonner_verb.why: English sound-alike painted in eglise/confessionnal (Nov 1 2026 EGLISE1 build): Monsieur Verbe, a cheerful slim mime with white face paint, a black-and-white horizontally striped shirt, black suspenders, black trousers, white gloves and a red beret, little motion lines around his hands, bending toward the sorry boy with open arms and a warm forgiving smile. Moved from the planned room ST_faith_seg001 (not yet built) into this room.
fr_pardonner_verb.note: This is a cognate: it looks and sounds close to the English word, so the picture simply shows it. Pardonner: to forgive (pardonner à quelqu'un). Pardon! is also 'Excuse me!' or 'Sorry?' when you didn't hear.

fr_peche_noun_2.why: English sound-alike painted in eglise/confessionnal (Nov 1 2026 EGLISE1 build): a boy about ten in a blue sweater sneaking a ripe orange-pink peach from a big wicker harvest-festival basket of fruit on a bench, glancing over his shoulder guiltily.
fr_peche_noun_2.note: Le péché is a sin; un péché mignon is a little weakness, a guilty pleasure (le chocolat, c'est mon péché mignon). Don't mix up la pêche (peach, fishing) or the verb pécher (to sin) and pêcher (to fish).

fr_confessionnal_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in eglise/confessionnal (Nov 1 2026 EGLISE1 build): a tall carved dark-oak confessional booth with three arched sections, a little door in the middle and purple velvet curtains on both sides, closed.
fr_confessionnal_noun.note: This is a cognate: it looks and sounds close to the English word, so the picture simply shows it. Le confessionnal is the booth where confession is heard.

fr_repentir_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in eglise/confessionnal (Nov 1 2026 EGLISE1 build): painter on a stepladder retouching a small framed landscape on the wall.
fr_repentir_noun.note: Le repentir is repentance, regret for a wrong. In art, un repentir is a painter's correction, a change painted over (visible under X-rays). The verb se repentir: to repent.

fr_marraine_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in eglise/baptistere (Nov 1 2026 EGLISE1 build): a smiling young woman in a pale-pink dress and a light raincoat hurrying in, shaking water off a dripping yellow umbrella, raindrops flying.
fr_marraine_noun.note: La marraine is the godmother; also the sponsor of a ship, a project or a new member (la marraine d'un navire).

fr_celebrer_verb.why: English sound-alike painted in eglise/baptistere (Nov 1 2026 EGLISE1 build): Monsieur Verbe, a cheerful slim mime with white face paint, a black-and-white horizontally striped shirt, black suspenders, black trousers, white gloves and a red beret, little motion lines around his hands, happily tossing a handful of pastel pink and blue sugared almonds into the air from a little white paper cone, three delighted children catching them. Moved from the planned room ST_faith_seg002 (not yet built) into this room.
fr_celebrer_verb.note: This is a cognate: it looks and sounds close to the English word, so the picture simply shows it. Célébrer: to celebrate (a party, a birthday) and also to celebrate Mass (le prêtre célèbre la messe), or to praise someone (célébrer un héros).

fr_fonts_baptismaux_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in eglise/baptistere (Nov 1 2026 EGLISE1 build): priest pouring water from a silver jug into the big stone font.
fr_fonts_baptismaux_noun.note: This is a cognate: it looks and sounds close to the English word, so the picture simply shows it. Les fonts baptismaux (always plural) is the baptismal font. Tenir un enfant sur les fonts baptismaux: to be a child's godparent; figuratively, to launch something new.

fr_chreme_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in eglise/baptistere (Nov 1 2026 EGLISE1 build): a small silver lidded jar on a little side table with a white cloth, a ginger cat on the table sniffing the jar hopefully, whiskers forward.
fr_chreme_noun.note: Le saint chrême is holy chrism, the scented oil used at baptism and confirmation. Close to English 'chrism'.

fr_bapteme_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in eglise/baptistere (Nov 1 2026 EGLISE1 build): a gray-haired grandfather carrying a happy baby in a long white christening gown, the baby waving a yellow bath sponge.
fr_bapteme_noun.note: Le baptême is a baptism (christening). Le baptême de l'air: your first flight in a plane; le baptême du feu: baptism of fire, a first battle or ordeal.

fr_parrain_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in eglise/baptistere (Nov 1 2026 EGLISE1 build): a young man in a gray suit running in out of breath, red-cheeked, one hand on his knee, holding a tall white decorated baptism candle.
fr_parrain_noun.note: Le parrain is the godfather; also a sponsor or mentor (le parrain d'une promotion), and in films, a mafia boss (le Parrain: The Godfather).

fr_tombe_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in eglise/cimetiere (Nov 1 2026 EGLISE1 build): a woman in a blue cardigan kneeling to plant a pot of fresh pink and white flowers on a neat grave with a simple gray headstone, a watering can beside her. Moved from the planned room R_mountain_02 (not yet built) into this room.
fr_tombe_noun.note: This is a cognate: it looks and sounds close to the English word, so the picture simply shows it. La tombe is a grave. Tomber (to fall) is a different word: il tombe means 'he falls'.

fr_pierre_tombale_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in eglise/cimetiere (Nov 1 2026 EGLISE1 build): a stonemason in a cap and canvas apron kneeling to gently brush green moss off an old gray rounded headstone with a soft brush, a little bucket beside him.
fr_pierre_tombale_noun.note: La pierre tombale is the headstone, gravestone: pierre = stone, tombale = of the tomb.

fr_epitaphe_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in eglise/cimetiere (Nov 1 2026 EGLISE1 build): girl tracing the face of an old headstone with her fingertip, grandpa standing behind.
fr_epitaphe_noun.note: This is a cognate: it looks and sounds close to the English word, so the picture simply shows it. Une épitaphe is the words carved on a tomb.

fr_cimetiere_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in eglise/cimetiere (Nov 1 2026 EGLISE1 build): a gardener in green overalls raking the gravel path between two tidy rows of old gray headstones with flowers. Moved from the planned room R_ch_crypt (not yet built) into this room.
fr_cimetiere_noun.note: This is a cognate: it looks and sounds close to the English word, so the picture simply shows it. Le cimetière is the cemetery; around a church, the churchyard. Un cimetière de voitures: a car scrapyard.

fr_caveau_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in eglise/cimetiere (Nov 1 2026 EGLISE1 build): small ivy-covered stone family vault with an arched wooden door, a boy beside it.
fr_caveau_noun.note: Le caveau is a family burial vault. Also a small cellar or a cellar club where music is played (un caveau de jazz).

fr_calvaire_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in eglise/cimetiere (Nov 1 2026 EGLISE1 build): a tall plain gray granite cross with no figure on it, standing on a three-stepped stone pedestal near the gate, a few wild flowers at its base. Moved from the planned room R_ch_altar_02 (not yet built) into this room.
fr_calvaire_noun.note: This is a cognate: it looks and sounds close to the English word, so the picture simply shows it. Un calvaire is a wayside cross (common in Brittany) or the hill of Calvary; figuratively, an ordeal (ce voyage a été un calvaire). Quebec French also uses it as a swear word.

fr_baptistere_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in eglise/baptistere (Nov 1 2026 EGLISE2): the round domed room and its small window with a dove, above the font.
fr_baptistere_noun.note: This is a cognate: it looks and sounds close to the English word, so the picture simply shows it. Le baptistère is a baptistery, the room or chapel with the font where baptisms take place.

fr_liturgie_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in eglise/choeur (Nov 1 2026 EGLISE2 build): a gray-haired woman cantor about sixty in a dark-blue dress standing at a small reading desk, holding a big open booklet with a red ribbon and raising one hand to lead the singing. Moved from the planned room R_ch_altar_02 (not yet built) into this room.
fr_liturgie_noun.note: This is a cognate: it looks and sounds close to the English word, so the picture simply shows it. La liturgie is the liturgy, the official order of public worship (la liturgie de la messe).

fr_consecration_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in eglise/choeur (Nov 1 2026 EGLISE2 build): priest in a green chasuble raising the host above the altar, server kneeling with a little bell. Moved from the planned room R_ch_altar_02 (not yet built) into this room.
fr_consecration_noun.note: This is a cognate: it looks and sounds close to the English word, so the picture simply shows it. La consécration is the moment of Mass when the bread and wine are consecrated; also the consecration of a church or a bishop, and figuratively a crowning success (la consécration d'un artiste).

fr_offrande_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in eglise/choeur (Nov 1 2026 EGLISE2 build): a girl about seven in a yellow cardigan carrying a big wicker basket full of round bread loaves and red apples toward the altar step with both hands, smiling proudly. Moved from the planned room R_ch_altar_02 (not yet built) into this room.
fr_offrande_noun.note: Une offrande is an offering or gift (to God, or to a cause): offrir = to offer. Not to be confused with l'offertoire, the moment of Mass when the gifts are brought up.

fr_encenser_verb.why: English sound-alike painted in eglise/choeur (Nov 1 2026 EGLISE2 build): Monsieur Verbe, a cheerful slim mime with white face paint, a black-and-white horizontally striped shirt, black suspenders, black trousers, white gloves and a red beret, little motion lines around his hands standing a little apart from the altar and gently swinging a brass censer on three chains, soft white incense smoke curling up. Moved from the planned room ST_faith_seg004 (not yet built) into this room.
fr_encenser_verb.note: This is a cognate: it looks and sounds close to the English word, so the picture simply shows it. Encenser = to cense, to burn incense toward someone or something. Figuratively, to flatter, to praise to the skies (la critique l'a encensé: the critics raved about him).

fr_liturgique_adj.why: English sound-alike painted in eglise/choeur (Nov 1 2026 EGLISE2 build): tall green banner with a gold circle on a wooden stand. Moved from the planned room R_ch_altar_02 (not yet built) into this room.
fr_liturgique_adj.note: This is a cognate: it looks and sounds close to the English word, so the picture simply shows it. Liturgique = liturgical: les couleurs liturgiques (green, white, purple, red), un chant liturgique.

fr_glorifier_verb.why: English sound-alike painted in eglise/choeur (Nov 1 2026 EGLISE2 build): mime in a red beret in the foreground with both arms flung up, singing. Moved from the planned room ST_faith_seg003 (not yet built) into this room.
fr_glorifier_verb.note: This is a cognate: it looks and sounds close to the English word, so the picture simply shows it. Glorifier = to glorify, to praise (glorifier Dieu); se glorifier de = to boast about.

fr_exhorter_verb.why: English sound-alike painted in eglise/choeur (Nov 1 2026 EGLISE2 build): mime in a red beret in front of the choir stalls raising one hand to urge the singers on. Moved from the planned room ST_cognition_seg014 (not yet built) into this room.
fr_exhorter_verb.note: This is a cognate: it looks and sounds close to the English word, so the picture simply shows it. Exhorter = to exhort, to urge strongly (exhorter quelqu'un à la patience).

fr_choeur_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in eglise/choeur (Nov 1 2026 EGLISE2 build): five choir singers of different ages in long white robes standing in the carved dark-oak choir stalls, singing from black music folders. New entry (EGLISE2), added for the funeral and church words.
fr_choeur_noun.note: Le chœur is a choir (the singers) and also the choir/chancel of a church, the part around the altar. Same Greek root as English chorus and choir. En chœur = in unison, all together.

fr_orgue_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in eglise/choeur (Nov 1 2026 EGLISE2 build): a big pipe organ high on the right wall: tall silver pipes in a carved wooden case on a small wooden gallery, an organist seen from behind at the keyboard. New entry (EGLISE2), added for the funeral and church words.
fr_orgue_noun.note: This is a cognate: it looks and sounds close to the English word, so the picture simply shows it. L'orgue is masculine in the singular (un bel orgue) but often feminine in the plural for one big church organ (les grandes orgues). Un orgue de Barbarie: a barrel organ.

fr_retable_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in eglise/tresor (Nov 1 2026 EGLISE2 build): big carved altarpiece with three painted flower panels above a white-clothed altar table, restorer on a ladder. Moved from the planned room R_ch_altar_02_z1 (not yet built) into this room.

fr_ciboire_noun.note: This is a cognate: it looks and sounds close to the English word, so the picture simply shows it. Le ciboire is the ciborium, the lidded cup that holds the Hosts.

fr_missel_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in eglise/tresor (Nov 1 2026 EGLISE2 build): a young bookbinder about thirty with rolled sleeves stitching a new red leather cover onto a very big old book with gold edges and ribbon markers.

fr_ambon_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in eglise/tresor (Nov 1 2026 EGLISE2 build): tall carved oak reading stand with a slanted top. Moved from the planned room R_ch_altar_02_z1 (not yet built) into this room.
fr_ambon_noun.note: This is a cognate: it looks and sounds close to the English word, so the picture simply shows it. L'ambon is the ambo, the fixed stand where the Bible readings are read.

fr_merci_noun_f.why: English sound-alike painted in eglise/misericorde (Nov 1 2026 EGLISE2 build): a girl about eight cupping both hands around a single small white candle flame that bends sideways in a draft from the door, protecting it. fr_misericorde_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in eglise/misericorde (Nov 1 2026 EGLISE2 build): painting of a shepherd with a crook freeing a little woolly white lamb from the brambles. Moved from the planned room R_ch_confessional (not yet built) into this room.
fr_misericorde_noun.note: La miséricorde is mercy, compassion (misère = misery + cœur = heart: a heart for those in misery). La Divine Miséricorde = Divine Mercy. Crier miséricorde = to beg for mercy.

fr_absolution_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in eglise/misericorde (Nov 1 2026 EGLISE2 build): seated priest in a purple stole raising his hand over a kneeling man. Moved from the planned room R_ch_confessional (not yet built) into this room.
fr_absolution_noun.note: This is a cognate: it looks and sounds close to the English word, so the picture simply shows it. L'absolution is the forgiveness of sins given by a priest after confession; in law, a discharge.

fr_penitence_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in eglise/misericorde (Nov 1 2026 EGLISE2 build): woman in a headscarf kneeling in a pew with folded hands. Moved from the planned room R_ch_confessional (not yet built) into this room.
fr_penitence_noun.note: La pénitence is penance, the prayer or good deed given after confession; also repentance. Second sense: a punishment (être en pénitence: to be grounded or in time-out). English penitence is a close cousin.

fr_misericordieux_adj.why: English sound-alike painted in eglise/misericorde (Nov 1 2026 EGLISE2 build): white-haired man wrapping his red scarf around a tired young man and giving him a sandwich.
fr_misericordieux_adj.note: Miséricordieux (miséricordieuse) = merciful, from miséricorde (mercy). Heureux les miséricordieux: blessed are the merciful.

fr_divin_adj.why: English sound-alike painted in eglise/misericorde (Nov 1 2026 EGLISE2 build): the high round window glowing bright gold, with wide soft beams of golden light pouring down from it toward the altar.
fr_divin_adj.note: This is a cognate: it looks and sounds close to the English word, so the picture simply shows it. Divin = divine, of God (la grâce divine). Second sense: exquisite, heavenly (ce gâteau est divin).

fr_absoudre_verb.why: English sound-alike painted in eglise/misericorde (Nov 1 2026 EGLISE2 build): mime in a golden-yellow beret scrubbing a chalk slate clean with a soapy sponge. Moved from the planned room ST_emotion_seg017 (not yet built) into this room.
fr_absoudre_verb.note: Absoudre = to absolve (forgive sins), also to acquit in court. Irregular: j'absous, nous absolvons; past participle absous, absoute.

fr_adorer_verb.why: English sound-alike painted in eglise/misericorde (Nov 1 2026 EGLISE2 build): Monsieur Verbe, a cheerful slim mime with white face paint, a black-and-white horizontally striped shirt, black suspenders, black trousers, white gloves and a red beret, little motion lines around his hands kneeling on a low wooden kneeler with his gloved hands folded, gazing up reverently toward the golden monstrance on the altar. fr_adorer_verb.note: This is a cognate: it looks and sounds close to the English word, so the picture simply shows it. Adorer = to adore, to worship (adorer Dieu); in everyday French, to love something (j'adore le chocolat).

fr_ostensoir_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in eglise/misericorde (Nov 1 2026 EGLISE2 build): a tall golden sunburst monstrance with long straight golden rays around a small round glass window holding a white host, standing on the stone altar between two candles. Moved from the planned room R_ch_altar_02 (not yet built) into this room.
fr_ostensoir_noun.note: L'ostensoir is a monstrance, the golden stand that shows the Host for adoration. From Latin ostendere (to show), like English ostensible and ostentatious.

fr_confesser_verb.why: English sound-alike painted in eglise/misericorde (Nov 1 2026 EGLISE2 build): Monsieur Verbe, a cheerful slim mime with white face paint, a black-and-white horizontally striped shirt, black suspenders, black trousers, white gloves and a red beret, little motion lines around his hands by the little food table at the back, pointing at himself with an embarrassed grin, cookie crumbs on his chin, holding up an empty round cookie tin. fr_confesser_verb.note: This is a cognate: it looks and sounds close to the English word, so the picture simply shows it. Confesser = to confess, to admit (confesser une faute); se confesser = to go to confession.

fr_purgatoire_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in eglise/misericorde (Nov 1 2026 EGLISE2 build): small side table with a row of lit red candles, an old woman praying behind it. Moved from the planned room R_ch_crypt (not yet built) into this room.
fr_purgatoire_noun.note: This is a cognate: it looks and sounds close to the English word, so the picture simply shows it. Le purgatoire is purgatory, in Catholic belief a state of cleansing before heaven; people light candles and pray for the souls there. Figuratively, a time of waiting and trial.

fr_eucharistie_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in eglise/salle (Nov 1 2026 EGLISE2 build): poster of a round loaf and a golden chalice with grapes on an easel. Moved from the planned room R_ch_altar_02 (not yet built) into this room.
fr_eucharistie_noun.note: This is a cognate: it looks and sounds close to the English word, so the picture simply shows it. L'eucharistie is the Eucharist, Holy Communion (from Greek 'thanksgiving').

fr_confirmation_noun.note: This is a cognate: it looks and sounds close to the English word, so the picture simply shows it. La confirmation is the sacrament of confirmation; also confirmation in general (la confirmation d'une réservation).

fr_onction_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in eglise/salle (Nov 1 2026 EGLISE2 build): old priest with his hand on a boy's head, the boy holding a small glass bottle of oil.
fr_onction_noun.note: L'onction is an anointing with holy oil (l'onction des malades: anointing of the sick); English unction. Second sense: a smooth, overly sweet manner (parler avec onction).

fr_catechumene_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in eglise/salle (Nov 1 2026 EGLISE2 build): young man writing in a notebook beside an open book at a back table.

fr_baptiser_verb.why: English sound-alike painted in eglise/salle (Nov 1 2026 EGLISE2 build): mime in a red beret pouring a little water over a baby doll in a metal basin. Moved from the planned room ST_faith_seg002 (not yet built) into this room.
fr_baptiser_verb.note: This is a cognate: it looks and sounds close to the English word, so the picture simply shows it. Baptiser = to baptize; also to name or christen something (baptiser un bateau, baptiser son chat Minou).

fr_communier_verb.why: English sound-alike painted in eglise/salle (Nov 1 2026 EGLISE2 build): mime in a red beret holding a little piece of bread in his cupped hands. Moved from the planned room ST_faith_seg004 (not yet built) into this room.
fr_communier_verb.note: This is a cognate: it looks and sounds close to the English word, so the picture simply shows it. Communier = to receive Communion; figuratively, to share deeply (communier dans la même passion).

fr_catholicisme_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in eglise/salle (Nov 1 2026 EGLISE2 build): big desk globe beside a tray of tiny red church models. Moved from the planned room R_ch_altar_02 (not yet built) into this room.

fr_canonisation_noun.note: This is a cognate: it looks and sounds close to the English word, so the picture simply shows it. La canonisation is canonization, when the Church declares someone a saint. Canoniser = to canonize.

fr_bienheureux_adj.why: English sound-alike painted in eglise/saints (Nov 1 2026 EGLISE2 build): white-bearded old man on a bench smelling a red rose with a blissful smile.
fr_bienheureux_adj.note: Bienheureux = blissful, very happy (literally 'well happy'); in church language, blessed (les Béatitudes: Heureux les...). Le bienheureux X: the Blessed X, a beatified person.

fr_venerer_verb.why: English sound-alike painted in eglise/saints (Nov 1 2026 EGLISE2 build): mime in a red beret bowing deeply with one hand on his heart. Moved from the planned room ST_faith_seg004 (not yet built) into this room.
fr_venerer_verb.note: This is a cognate: it looks and sounds close to the English word, so the picture simply shows it. Vénérer = to venerate, to revere (vénérer les saints); also to deeply admire a person.

fr_vouer_verb.why: English sound-alike painted in eglise/saints (Nov 1 2026 EGLISE2 build): Monsieur Verbe, a cheerful slim mime with white face paint, a black-and-white horizontally striped shirt, black suspenders, black trousers, white gloves and a red beret, little motion lines around his hands on tiptoe hanging one small silver heart-shaped plaque on a nail among dozens of others on the wall, looking pleased. fr_pelerin_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in eglise/saints (Nov 1 2026 EGLISE2 build): a pilgrim man about forty with a tall wooden walking staff, a wide-brimmed hat, a backpack with a white scallop shell tied on, and dusty boots. New entry (EGLISE2), added for the funeral and church words.

fr_sanctuaire_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in eglise/saints (Nov 1 2026 EGLISE2 build): a stone wall niche shrine with a small statue of the bearded gardener monk holding a spade, surrounded by pots of red roses and little lit candles. fr_sanctuaire_noun.note: This is a cognate: it looks and sounds close to the English word, so the picture simply shows it. Le sanctuaire is a sanctuary: the holy place around the altar, a shrine or place of pilgrimage (le sanctuaire de Lourdes), or a refuge for animals.

fr_archange_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in eglise/saints (Nov 1 2026 EGLISE2 build): stained-glass archangel with white wings and a red robe. New entry (EGLISE2), added for the funeral and church words.
fr_archange_noun.note: This is a cognate: it looks and sounds close to the English word, so the picture simply shows it. Un archange is an archangel (l'archange Gabriel, Michel, Raphaël).

fr_aspirer_verb.why: English sound-alike painted in eglise/saints (Nov 1 2026 EGLISE2 build): mime in a red beret pushing an old upright vacuum cleaner over a trail of rose petals in front of the tapestry. Moved from the planned room ST_emotion_seg014 (not yet built) into this room.
fr_aspirer_verb.note: Aspirer = to suck up, to breathe in (aspirer de l'air), to vacuum (un aspirateur: a vacuum cleaner). Second sense: aspirer à = to aspire to (aspirer à la paix). English aspirate and aspire share the Latin root (to breathe).

fr_funerailles_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in eglise/portail (Nov 1 2026 EGLISE2 build): calm group of adults in dark clothes holding white flowers. New entry (EGLISE2), added for the funeral and church words.
fr_funerailles_noun.note: This is a cognate: it looks and sounds close to the English word, so the picture simply shows it. Les funérailles (always plural, feminine) are a funeral, formal word: des funérailles nationales (a state funeral).

fr_obseques_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in eglise/portail (Nov 1 2026 EGLISE2 build): small table with a white cloth, an open book and a vase of white lilies. New entry (EGLISE2), added for the funeral and church words.
fr_obseques_noun.note: Les obsèques (always plural, feminine) are a funeral, the formal word used in notices and invitations (les obsèques auront lieu mardi). English obsequies is the same word.

fr_recueillir_verb.why: English sound-alike painted in eglise/portail (Nov 1 2026 EGLISE2 build): mime in a golden-yellow beret gathering fallen white lilies into a bouquet. Moved from the planned room ST_social_seg007 (not yet built) into this room.
fr_recueillir_verb.note: Recueillir = to collect, to gather (recueillir des signatures, des dons); to take in (recueillir un chat abandonné). fr_cercueil_noun.why: Plain picture painted in eglise/portail (Nov 1 2026 EGLISE2 build, EGLISE2b text): closed polished wooden casket covered with white roses on a wheeled stand. fr_cercueil_noun.note: Le cercueil is a coffin, a casket (mettre en bière = to place in the coffin). It comes from the same Greek word as English sarcophagus.

fr_enterrement_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in eglise/portail (Nov 1 2026 EGLISE2 build): grave site with a green cloth, white flower wreaths and a gray headstone. New entry (EGLISE2), added for the funeral and church words.
fr_enterrement_noun.note: L'enterrement is a burial, a funeral (aller à un enterrement); from enterrer = to bury, en + terre (earth), like English interment. Un enterrement de vie de garçon: a bachelor party.

fr_corbillard_noun.why: Plain picture painted in eglise/portail (Nov 1 2026 EGLISE2 build, EGLISE2b text); the same hearse is seen beyond the open gate in eglise/cimetiere. No vivid literal sound-alike that stays respectful, so the word is on HOOK_FORM_eglise2.tsv. New entry (EGLISE2), added for the funeral and church words.
fr_corbillard_noun.note: Le corbillard is a hearse. The name comes from the corbillats, the old passenger boats of the town of Corbeil.

fr_diacre_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in eglise/portail (Nov 1 2026 EGLISE2b fix): young deacon in a white alb with a diagonal stole, holding an open book, in front of the left gatepost. New entry (EGLISE2b), added on request with a plain picture.
fr_diacre_noun.note: This is a cognate: diacre and deacon come from the same Greek word (diakonos, servant), so the picture simply shows it. Un diacre is a deacon; a deacon wears his stole diagonally, from the left shoulder to the right hip.

fr_archeveque_noun.why: Plain picture painted in eglise/crypte (Nov 1 2026 EGLISE2b fix): low stone tomb with a recumbent carved archbishop (miter, folded hands, pallium with small crosses). New entry (EGLISE2b), added on request with a plain picture.
fr_archeveque_noun.note: No English sound-alike: a plain picture. Un archevêque is an archbishop: arch- (chief, as in archange) + évêque (bishop). The pallium, a white band with black crosses, is the archbishop's sign. L'archevêché = the archbishop's palace.

fr_catholique_adj.why: Plain picture in eglise/cimetiere: a wooden rosary on the gravel between the headstones. The cat-and-leek pun is gone.
fr_catholique_adj.note: Cognate of English Catholic. Catholique means Catholic, of the Roman Catholic Church (une école catholique; l'Église catholique). In the set phrase pas très catholique it means shady, not quite right (une affaire pas très catholique = a fishy business). Its opposite is protestant, or in the second sense honnête, net.
